newsitem.title: KYRGYZSTAN: Cameco outlines Kyrgyz Dzherui mine plan.
newsitem.headline: Cameco outlines Kyrgyz Dzherui mine plan.

text.p: Canada's Cameco Corp and Kyrgyz state concern Kyrgyzaltyn will start joint gold mining on the Dzherui field later this year, a Cameco official said on Monday.

Len Homeniuk, president of Kumtor Operating Company, which is managing a deal between Cameco and Kyrgyzaltyn on the Kumtor goldfield, told a news briefing that a feasibility study of the project was expected to be completed in June.
Dzherui, with gold reserves of 50 tonnes, is situated in Kyrgyzstan's Talas region, and is the Central Asian nation's second largest gold field.
Officials provided no further details of the project.
The Kumtor goldfield remains the largest joint venture in the former Soviet republic, and has gold reserves of 514 tonnes.
Cameco, better known as a large uranium producer, has invested $452 million in Kumtor. It owns one third of the mine. State-owned Kyrgyzaltyn owns the remaining two thirds.
